name: Jawmogging

lead: Jawmogging is community slang for outshining someone else specifically through jaw structure. "Mogging" means appearing superior to those around you, and "jaw" narrows it to the jawline.
It matters in looksmaxxing because a defined jaw is one of the features people check when assessing male faces. Most of the methods used to pursue it are covered in their own entries.

paras: People describe working on the jawline through leanness (lower body fat shows the jaw), grooming such as a beard, camera angles and posture, and for some, chewing, orthodontics, fillers, implants or jaw surgery. Each has a separate wiki entry.
Risks depend on the method used: surgical and injectable routes carry medical risks, and practices like jaw hammering have drawn warnings from surgeons. The term itself is only a comparison.

chain: Define the jaw through leanness, grooming, angles or structural procedures
angle.text: Jawmogging describes the outcome of a more defined jawline. People pursue it through many separate methods, from leaning out and grooming to chewing, fillers or surgery.

lead: Jawmogging is a looksmaxxing term for having a stronger jaw than someone else. It combines "mogging", slang for outshining others in appearance, confidence or status [1], with the jawline, which the Looksmaxxing article lists as a feature people check when rating men [2].

"Mogging" arose from "AMOG" (alpha male of the group) in online manosphere and incel communities and later shifted toward physical comparison [1][2]. Jawmogging applies that comparison to the jaw alone.
No studies have examined jawmogging as such.

paras: Jawmogging is the act or state of having a jaw that looks stronger than another person's. It is used both as praise for a prominent jaw and as a way to compare faces.
Mogging in general means superiority over others in appearance, confidence or status, and came from "AMOG" [1].

Surveys of the topic mention mewing (a tongue-posture technique) and bonesmashing; researchers say evidence for structural change from mewing is lacking, and surgeons have warned of fractures from bonesmashing [2]. Jaw surgery is classed under "hardmaxxing" [2].
